transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-24
Time: 14:00 - 14:55 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Maya, Diego, Priya (Redwood) / Liam, Sana, Arjun, Marta (Edencrest)
Links referenced: ref-arch deck: https://redwood.app/s/edn-refarch-deck, pilot spreadsheet: https://docs.redwood/app/edn-pilot-sheet

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): ok hey everyone thanks for joining, i'll kick off, we've got about 55 minutes on the calendar, goal is to align on the marketplace listing bar, the reference architecture for the hybrid gateway, and scope a pilot run, quick intros?
[00:20] Liam (Edencrest CTO): yeah hi liam here, i'll be owning the pilot with sana and marta on infra, arjun on security will chime in on kms, thanks for setting this up
[00:30] Maya: great, diego from our solutions team will walk through the ref-arch and latency/cost tradeoffs
[00:36] Diego (Redwood SE): hi all, thanks. i'll share my screen in a sec, but high level, we recommend a model of marketplace listing + hybrid adapter: customers can route live traffic to Redwood hosted endpoints, or to a private deployment (VPC) that you control, with canary routing to fallback models if capacity hits limits
[01:05] Sana (Head of Cloud Ops): quick Q on that, what does the VPC connectivity look like? we run in multiple cloud accounts and have strict egress policies
[01:15] Diego: good question. two common patterns: 1) VPC peering / private link where Redwood's private connector sits in your VPC and we fetch via private networking; 2) a centrally managed transit with restricted egress, optionally with a NAT box for metrics. peering preferred for isolation. note: peering requires some network setup and route tables, and there's an IP allowlist step on our side
[01:40] Marta (Platform Eng): when you say connector, is that an appliance we deploy or a managed agent?
[01:46] Diego: it's a lightweight connector image you deploy via helm to your cluster (onprem or cloud). it establishes an outbound TLS tunnel to Redwood control plane. nothing inbound required — that's the safety bit. we also offer a fully air-gapped option but that takes longer for onboarding
[02:15] Arjun (Security Architect): KMS is critical. we can't allow Redwood to hold plaintext keys. how does key management work?
[02:22] Priya (PM): we integrate with customer KMS — bring-your-own-key. Redwood can call your KMS for envelope keys; for HSM-backed workflows we have an HSM flow and audit logs. we'll share the KMS checklist after this call
[02:40] Arjun: ok, do you support AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, google?
[02:45] Maya: yes all three, plus some on-prem HSM partners. note: for marketplace listing there are docs we need to fill about key rotation and separation of duties, we'll attach that
[03:10] Liam: also need SSO/SAML and RBAC; our product owners insist on provisioning via SCIM ideally
[03:18] Maya: supported — SAML, SCIM for user provisioning and RBAC; we'll provide the SSO integration guide. for enterprise we can do dedicated tenant + role mappings
[03:40] Diego: shifting to performance: the main levers are model variant, quantization, and batching. for low-latency paths we suggest smaller model variants with fp16 or int8 quant, boxed into a dedicated pool for the pilot. for cost/throughput we can enable continuous batching and prefix caching
[04:05] Sana: what's the expected latency hit when enabling batching? our UX needs median p50 sub-120ms on chat turns
[04:12] Diego: median depends on instance type and sequence length. with an aggressive batching profile you might see 30-60ms extra per token under heavy load. with dedicated reserved capacity we can hit lower tail latencies — that's the tradeoff: cost vs 99th percentile latency. we can run microbenchmarks in the lab to estimate for your payloads
[04:46] Marta: microbenchmarks — great. what do you need from our side to run those?
[04:50] Diego: sample prompts, typical sequence lengths, concurrent users, and a representative rate curve. we'll also want CPU/GPU family preference — e.g., a100 vs h100 has different perf and quantization compatibility
[05:10] Liam: we primarily have A100s in prod but can test on h100s in sandbox if needed
[05:16] Diego: noted. another note: some open models have better int8 paths than others; we can recommend model+quant mix in the ref-arch deck. i'll call out which models have validated performance profiles in our catalog
[05:42] Sana: second security question — audit logs and data residency. we need full request/response audit trails for compliance, but certain payloads must never leave our VPC unencrypted
[05:52] Priya: we offer token-level audit logs and you can choose retention windows. for sensitive payloads we propose using enclave-style private deployments where everything is processed in your VPC and only metadata reaches Redwood control plane. we'll note this in the runbook
[06:20] Arjun: encryption at rest and in transit is fine, but can we do field-level redaction before it hits the logs?
[06:26] Diego: there's a built-in redaction preprocessor in the connector that can strip or hash fields client-side before sending to Redwood. it's configurable and we'll include sample configs in the repo
[06:40] Liam: about marketplace listing: what are the gating criteria? do we need a support SLA to list?
[06:48] Maya: for listing we require a minimum test checklist: VPC/KMS compatibility validated, packaging (helm chart) in our registry, automated e2e smoke tests, security questionnaire answered (and SOC2 doc). marketplace listing also asks for a billing integration piece if you want in-market billing — optional for pilot
[07:10] Marta: billing integration — we probably won't do in-market billing for pilot, just manual billing off the SOW
[07:15] Maya: that's fine, listing can be limited to discovery docs and a partner ref-arch without billing
[07:22] Diego: on the pilot scope: propose 4-week lab: week1 environment build, week2 bench tests + tuning, week3 canary traffic with synthetic load, week4 final report + go/no-go. success metrics: <120ms p50 for standard chat, acceptable cost per 1k tokens under defined baseline, and KMS integration validated
[07:50] Liam: that's workable. estimate of infra hours?
[07:55] Diego: roughly 40-60 engineering hours from Redwood side for the lab plus 20-30 hours from Edencrest infra depending on access level
[08:10] Arjun: single point: we need to ensure audit events are tamperproof. does your control plane maintain immutable logs?
[08:16] Priya: yes we stream signed audit events to the tenant's log sink; for private deployments you can direct logs to your own SIEM. we'll share the audit schema
[08:35] Sana: any PII handling guidance? we have SSNs and customer identifiers in some prompts
[08:40] Maya: default guidance is minimize PII in prompts. for those cases we recommend client-side tokenization/masking plus using private deployment. we'll add examples to the redaction guide
[09:05] Diego: circling back to model shipping: if you want the absolute lowest latency we can recommend a smaller distilled model hosted in dedicated pool. if accuracy matters more we pick larger models and enable KV cache and prefix optimization to reduce token regen
[09:30] Liam: curious about fallbacks — if dedicated capacity is saturated, does traffic drop or auto-failover?
[09:36] Diego: we have routing policies: fail-open to a hosted-compatible model or queue, or throttle with graceful degradation. you can set policy by route. for production customer apps we commonly configure canary routing + fallback to cheaper model family during spikes
[10:00] Marta: do you support per-route throttles and per-token cost tags? we need chargeback for internal teams
[10:06] Priya: yes route-level cost tagging, and console exposes token-level breakdowns, we can preconfigure dashboards for your tenancy
[10:20] Liam: storage of cached KV — where does that live? in your infra or ours?
[10:25] Diego: KV cache can be kept in the connector for private deployments (stays in your VPC) or in Redwood's cache for hosted. cache placement affects cold start and data residency
[10:45] Arjun: small item on legal: do you support contract language for data processing addendum and sub-processor lists?
[10:50] Maya: yes we'll provide DPA templates and current sub-processor list; legal can follow up with your counsel. i'll attach the DPA PDF after the call
[11:10] Diego: technical deep-dive: i'll sketch the ref-arch — (screen) connector helm chart in your cluster -> private endpoint -> secure tunnel to redwood control plane -> model servers in dedicated pools w/ autoscale -> observability via prometheus + trace hooks. canary routing sits in the control plane
[11:55] Marta: can the connector be configured to limit egress bandwidth and concurrent connections?
[11:58] Diego: yes limits in helm values; we can also rate-shape at route level. we'll provide example helm values for your scale
[12:25] Liam: about metrics and SLOs, can we get SLA-backed latency for dedicated pools?
[12:30] Maya: yes dedicated reserved capacity comes with SLA and defined latency targets; we'll include options in the SOW draft
[12:50] Sana: curious about the onboarding timeline — how long to get the VPC connector live?
[12:55] Diego: typically 2-3 business days for connector deploy + access validation, if there are no network policy blockers. full pilot readiness (bench tests, tuning) usually 2-4 weeks
[13:20] Arjun: on encryption, if we want to hold all ephemeral keys in our HSM, is there any runtime that requires Redwood to cache keys?
[13:28] Diego: no, we use envelope encryption — Redwood only gets encrypted keys; your KMS/HSM signs or unwraps on your side. for some lab flows we request temporary signing tokens but those can be ephemeral and audited
[13:55] Maya: quick note on quantization compat: some internal models your team uses may not quantize well, we will call that out in the model compatibility list. diego will mark which model families are validated for int8
[14:10] Diego: small demo of bench numbers (verbal): on a100, int8 quant with batching we saw 3x throughput improvement and 15-20% p50 latency reduction compared to fp16 under our traces; but accuracy delta needs verification for your prompts
[14:35] Liam: we need accuracy checks integrated into pilot, can you tie evals to alerts?
[14:40] Priya: yes we can wire prompt evaluation harness — we run eval sets and can trigger regression alerts if quality drops beyond threshold
[15:00] Marta: ok what's in the pilot report?
[15:03] Diego: performance tables, cost estimates, SLO attainment, security validation checklist, runbook for production rollout, and recommended listing artifacts
[15:25] Maya: let's confirm responsibilities: Redwood provides ref-arch deck, helm chart, bench playbook, SOC2 artifacts. Edencrest provides network diagram, KMS constraints, sample payloads. we'll capture dates in next steps
[15:45] Liam: agreed. also, any known behavioral differences if we run the connector in kubernetes vs a VM?
[15:52] Diego: kube is easiest for most customers; VM is supported but requires some extra config around systemd and container auth. we'll include both in the repo
[16:10] Arjun: one more security ask — can we get a pen-test summary on the connector?
[16:14] Priya: yes we have an internal security assessment and we can share an executive summary; for an enterprise pilot we can offer a joint pentest schedule
[16:30] Maya: moving to logistics — i'll draft a 4-week pilot SOW and circulate by EOD Wednesday (2026-08-26). diego will prep bench playbook, arjun and marta will exchange network/KMS docs
16:48 Liam: sounds good. any blockers we should call out now?
16:52 Sana: the only potential blocker is our compliance window — we need legal sign-off for DPA before any sample data leaves the VPC. that may add a week
17:05 Maya: noted, we'll mark pilot start conditional on DPA signed; we can run isolated bench tests with synthetic data in meantime
17:25 Diego: final item — we'll run a 2-hour lab with your infra team; propose 2026-09-02 09:00 UTC, is that OK?
17:32 Marta: tentative ok from our side, will confirm once we share calendar
17:40 Maya: great, recap next steps — i'll send pricing & SOW, diego bench playbook, redwood will share SOC2 + DPA templates, edencrest to share network + kms diagram. meet cadence: weekly check-in for pilot run
17:55 Liam: thanks all, this was super helpful
17:58 Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in thread and attach artifacts

[END]
